cards.explanation: The answer is False. Isaiah says the remnant "…will no longer depend on him who struck them…" (Isaiah 10:20). They stop leaning on the one who hit them. Picture a wobbly cooling rack that you finally quit setting hot pans on, friends. Something steadier is coming for them.

The answer is The LORD. Isaiah says they "…will truly rely on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel." (Isaiah 10:20). Notice the word truly, friends. This is leaning with your whole weight, not just a little lean. I always say a good oven earns that kind of trust.

The answer is that they are a huge number. Nobody counts sand at the beach, friends, it just goes on and on. Isaiah says "Though your people, O Israel, be like the sand of the sea, only a remnant will return." (Isaiah 10:22). So the picture is a crowd too big to count. And then comes the surprising turn.

The answer is the whole land. Isaiah says "…the Lord GOD of Hosts will carry out the destruction decreed upon the whole land." (Isaiah 10:23). This is a heavy verse, friends. The word that matters is whole.

The answer is Do not fear Assyria. The Lord says, "O My people who dwell in Zion, do not fear Assyria, who strikes you with a rod and lifts his staff against you as the Egyptians did." (Isaiah 10:24). Assyria is the one swinging the rod, and still the word is do not fear. That's a bold thing to hear when somebody is lifting a staff at you, bakers.

The answer is subside. The Lord says, "…in just a little while My fury against you will subside, and My anger will turn to their destruction." (Isaiah 10:25). Subside means it settles down, like a timer finally going quiet. Notice the little while, friends. The hard stretch has an end.

The answer is True. Isaiah says the LORD of Hosts "…will raise His staff over the sea, as He did in Egypt." (Isaiah 10:26). It's a look back to what the Lord already did there, friends. Isaiah points to it as the way things will go again.

The answer is neck. Isaiah says, "The yoke will be broken because your neck will be too large." (Isaiah 10:27). A yoke sits on the neck, so a neck too big snaps it right off, friends. The burden comes off the shoulders and the yoke off the neck.

The answer is True. Isaiah says, "Yet today they will halt at Nob, shaking a fist at the mount of Daughter Zion, at the hill of Jerusalem." (Isaiah 10:32). After all those towns, the march halts at Nob, friends. Then comes the fist, and I can feel the tension.

The answer is Jerusalem. The fist shakes "…at the mount of Daughter Zion, at the hill of Jerusalem." (Isaiah 10:32). Zion and Jerusalem are the same hill in that line, bakers. All those towns fleeing, and then comes the fist at Jerusalem's hill.

The answer is cut down. Isaiah says, "The tall trees will be cut down, the lofty ones will be felled." (Isaiah 10:33). The Lord lops off the branches with terrifying power, and the tall trees come down, friends. The picture shifts from a marching army to a forest.

The answer is False. Isaiah says, "…Lebanon will fall before the Mighty One." (Isaiah 10:34). It comes after the axe clears the forest thickets, friends. Lebanon doesn't stand firm, it falls before the Mighty One.
